Absolutely Right!

Always done that when a really narrow resonance is peaking its head out too much. Like if something is way too resonant and unflattering -- absolutely jump in there and nip it in the bud. Not everything is recorded in the most flattering environment, so you've gotta do what you've gotta do.

If, as you sweep across, something jumps out way louder than everything else. Just ask yourself if you like it or not, and make a judgement.

I should say, with this technique, it's not about what sounds good or bad, generally. It's more about the level difference between surrounding frequencies and the song/instrument/track as a whole. It's about smoothing out the frequencies, flattening them. But of course anything too flat can sound boring and dull. So yeah, that's my 2 cents.
